title: 2024 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: Integers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) satisfy \(ab+c=100,\) \(bc+a=87,\) and \(ca+b=60.\) What is \(ab+bc+ca?\)

solutions.text: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \((a-c)(b-1)=13.\) Hence \[ \begin{gathered} (a-c,b-1)\in\{(1,13),(13,1),\\ (-1,-13),(-13,-1)\}. \end{gathered} \] The corresponding values of \(b\) are \(14,2,-12,0.\) Substituting \(a=c+(a-c)\) into \(ab+c=100\) eliminates the first two cases because they would require \(15c=86\) or \(3c=74.\) The case \(b=-12\) gives \(c=-8\) and \(a=-9,\) which satisfies all three equations. The case \(b=0\) gives \((a,c)=(87,100),\) which fails \(ca+b=60.\) Thus the unique integer solution is \((-9,-12,-8),\) and \(ab+bc+ca\) \(=108+96+72=276.\) Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Subtract equations in pairs, e.g. \((ab+c)-(bc+a)\) factors as \((a-c)(b-1)=13\)
\(13\) is prime, so \((a-c,\ b-1)\) has few options; test them for integer solutions
